step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Philosopher Frank Ramsey, who died in 1930 aged 26

step5_concept_grounding: Retrospective speculative discussion of Weil's disease (leptospirosis) as an unverified historical hypothesis for death in 1930

rationale: A historical biographical case report exploring speculative retrospective causes of death for philosopher Frank Ramsey, who died in 1930. The final contemporaneous death certificate recorded cholangitis and hepatitis. Leptospirosis (Weil's disease) is mentioned solely as a modern retrospective hypothesis in the abstract and discussion, without clinical or diagnostic verification in the patient during life. Excluded as non-target case.

rationale: A 35-year-old pregnant woman (36 weeks gestation) presented with fever, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, oliguria, and multivisceral failure. Leptospira IgM antibodies by ELISA were positive at 1/300 dilution, confirming severe leptospirosis (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 50-year-old male sushi chef presenting with severe pulmonary hemorrhagic syndrome requiring VV-ECMO

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira interrogans confirmed by fourfold rise in paired serum antibody titers

evidence_items.source_quote: Finally, paired serum antibody titer testing (on days 5 and 19 after the onset of symptoms) showed a fourfold or higher increase in antibody titers for Leptospira interrogans serovar Copenhageni and Leptospira interrogans serovar Icterohaemorrhagiae, confirming the diagnosis of leptospirosis.
evidence_items.target_concept: Leptospira interrogans serovars Copenhageni and Icterohaemorrhagiae

rationale: A 50-year-old sushi chef presented with jaundice, renal failure, and life-threatening diffuse alveolar hemorrhage managed with VV-ECMO. Paired serology between days 5 and 19 showed a fourfold or higher titer increase for L. interrogans Copenhageni and Icterohaemorrhagiae, fulfilling E1 confirmatory criteria. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 65-year-old male Swiss fisherman presenting with septic shock, multiple-organ failure, and myocarditis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira icterohaemorrhagiae confirmed by positive serology

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies for Leptospira icterohaemorrhagiae were positive, confirming the diagnosis.

rationale: A 65-year-old fisherman presented with fever, jaundice, troponin elevation, and multiorgan failure successfully managed with high-volume hemofiltration and plasma exchange. Serology for Leptospira icterohaemorrhagiae was positive, confirming the diagnosis (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 45-year-old male farmer presenting with severe icterus, cardiomyopathy, and ventricular arrhythmias following floodwater exposure

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by serological testing

evidence_items.source_quote: Eventually, his serologies returned positive for leptospirosis infection (Table 1).

rationale: A 45-year-old farmer presented with severe icterus, new-onset cardiomyopathy (EF 30-35%), and malignant arrhythmias following flood water exposure. Serological testing was positive for leptospirosis, confirming fulminant infection (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old male presenting with fever, jaundice, and AKI, initially suspected of leptospirosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as working diagnosis and ruled out by negative antibody and PCR assays

evidence_items.source_quote: Later on, antibody and PCR assays for Leptospira were negative. F. necrophorum was isolated in blood cultures on the second day.
evidence_items.test_name: Antibody and PCR assays for Leptospira

rationale: A 38-year-old male presented with fever, severe jaundice, and anuric AKI mimicking Weil's disease. Specific Leptospira antibody and PCR assays were negative, while blood cultures confirmed Fusobacterium necrophorum bacteremia. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old male presenting with acute febrile illness, arthralgia, and myalgia evaluated for leptospirosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as endemic differential and tested negative by IgM and IgG serology

evidence_items.source_quote: leptospira IgM and IgG performed on day 7 were negative.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presented with acute febrile illness and multiorgan involvement. Leptospira IgM and IgG performed on day 7 were negative, whereas hantavirus IgM was repeatedly positive. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 37-year-old male farmer presenting with fever, ARDS, and respiratory failure

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as endemic differential and tested negative by IgM serology

evidence_items.source_quote: Dengue IgM and leptospirosis IgM done on day 6 illness were negative.

rationale: A 37-year-old farmer presented with fever, dyspnea, and ARDS. Leptospirosis IgM serology on day 6 was negative, and hantavirus IgM was positive on days 3 and 25. Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old male fishery officer and rice paddy worker presenting with intracranial hemorrhage and jaundice

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by positive serum IgM-ELISA

evidence_items.source_quote: leptospirosis was clinically suspected, which was further confirmed by the positive serum IgM-ELISA (IgG value of 100 and an IgM value of 20).

rationale: A 51-year-old rice paddy worker presented with fever, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, and temporoparietal intracranial hemorrhage. Diagnosis was confirmed by positive serum IgM-ELISA (IgM 20, IgG 100) (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A female red panda (Ailurus fulgens) at a zoo with Leptospira kirschneri infection

step5_concept_grounding: Isolation and whole genome sequencing of Leptospira kirschneri serovar Grippotyphosa from a red panda

evidence_items.source_quote: On August 3, the red panda began to show abnormal behavior and was reported as lethargic, anorexic, with abdominal discomfort and vomiting (Figure 1).

rationale: A veterinary case report detailing the clinical presentation, urinary culture, and genome sequencing of Leptospira kirschneri in a zoo red panda (Ailurus fulgens). Veterinary and non-human cases are excluded from the human clinical gold standard -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 33-year-old male presenting with acute oxidative hemolysis and AKI due to G6PD deficiency after herbal remedy

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated in acute hepatonephritis and ruled out by negative PCR and paired MAT

evidence_items.source_quote: Leptospiral polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was negative and paired leptospiral microscopic agglutination test (MAT) did not demonstrate a fourfold rise and neither of the titers were significant.

rationale: A 33-year-old male developed dark urine, jaundice, and anuric AKI following ingestion of an Acalypha herbal remedy. Leptospirosis was evaluated and excluded with negative PCR and paired MAT showing no significant titers, while acute G6PD-mediated oxidative hemolysis was confirmed. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 4-year-old female spayed American Bulldog evaluated for copper-associated hepatitis

step5_concept_grounding: Veterinary clinical report of canine copper-associated hepatitis with negative Leptospira titers

evidence_items.source_quote: A 4-year-old, female spayed American Bulldog presented to the Clinical Nutrition Service at the Ontario Veterinary College's Health Sciences Center for a homemade diet (HMD) formulation for the nutritional management of hepatic enzymopathy and suspected Cu-associated hepatitis.

rationale: A veterinary clinical case report on the nutritional management of an American Bulldog presenting with hepatic enzymopathy. Veterinary animal subjects are excluded from the human clinical gold standard -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 73-year-old male presenting with severe pulmonary hemorrhage and invasive pulmonary aspergillosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira interrogans confirmed by BAL mNGS in coinfection with Aspergillus flavus

evidence_items.source_quote: Three days later, mNGS showed seven sequence numbers of Leptospira interrogans and 1,289,906 sequences of Aspergillus flavus.

rationale: A 73-year-old male presented with fever, hemoptysis, and respiratory failure. Metagenomic NGS of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid detected seven sequence reads of Leptospira interrogans along with Aspergillus flavus, confirming pulmonary hemorrhagic leptospirosis complicated by aspergillosis (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 38-year-old female presenting with muscle pain, night sweats, facial rash, and AKI

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira interrogans serovar Bratislava confirmed by MAT at 1/800 titer

evidence_items.source_quote: the leptospira MAT test performed at the Spirochet Diseases Diagnosis Laboratory of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Veterinary Control Central Research Institute revealed antibodies against L. interrogans serovar Bratislava type strain Jez Bratislava at 1/800 titer in the patient (Figure 1). Thus, a definitive diagnosis of leptospirosis was made.

rationale: A 38-year-old female presented with muscle pain, fever, facial erythema, and acute kidney impairment after animal contact. Reference laboratory MAT revealed high-titer antibodies (1/800) against Leptospira interrogans serovar Bratislava, establishing a definitive diagnosis (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 41-year-old male presenting with jaundice, AKI, and ascending lower limb weakness (AIDP)

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis complicated by AIDP confirmed by positive serum IgM ELISA

evidence_items.source_quote: His serum Leptospira Enzyme Linked Immunosorbant Assay (ELISA) IgM was positive (titre of 3.8).

rationale: A 41-year-old male living in an informal settlement without municipal sanitation presented with jaundice, AKI, and acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP). Serum Leptospira IgM ELISA was positive (titer 3.8), and he made a full recovery following IV ceftriaxone (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old female presenting with altered sensorium, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed in coinfection with Dengue virus

evidence_items.source_quote: Day 1 reports (Tables 1, 2) suggested dengue and Leptospira coinfection fever with mild hepatitis and thrombocytopenia.

rationale: A 51-year-old female presented with fever, altered sensorium, thrombocytopenia, and multiorgan dysfunction. Day 1 investigations confirmed acute coinfection of Dengue and Leptospira, and she was treated with IV doxycycline and recovered (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 36-year-old male gardener in a rodent-infested settlement presenting with profound jaundice and conjunctival suffusion

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by positive Leptospira IgM serology

evidence_items.source_quote: On day eight, the Leptospira IgM was positive. The patient was discharged after 10 days of ceftriaxone when haemodynamically stable, apyrexial and mobilising in the ward.

rationale: A 36-year-old male gardener living in an informal settlement infested with rodents presented with fever, prominent conjunctival suffusion, severe jaundice, and AKI. Leptospira IgM returned positive on day eight, confirming Weil's disease (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 31-year-old male presenting with fever, jaundice, and multiple splenic/liver abscesses

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis evaluated as part of acute febrile illness panel and tested negative

evidence_items.source_quote: He had been hospitalized at another facility for a week, where tests for dengue, leptospirosis, scrub typhus, and typhoid were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Serologic panel for acute febrile illness

rationale: A 31-year-old male presented with fever, jaundice, and altered consciousness due to multiple visceral abscesses. Testing for leptospirosis was negative, and blood cultures subsequently confirmed Burkholderia pseudomallei (melioidosis). Target disease was tested and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 51-year-old male presenting with severe pulmonary hemorrhage and respiratory failure requiring VV-ECMO

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira confirmed by blood mNGS in coinfection with Influenza A (H1N1)

evidence_items.source_quote: The mNGS of blood only indicates a possibility of Leptospira infection (blood reads 2).

rationale: A 51-year-old male developed jaundice, AKI, and diffuse airway hemorrhage after fishing in the rain. Metagenomic NGS of blood detected Leptospira sequences, and targeted penicillin therapy with VV-ECMO led to complete clinical recovery (E1). True coinfection with H1N1. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 55-year-old male paddy field worker presenting with severe pulmonary hemorrhage and bowel necrosis

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by microscopic agglutination test (MAT)

evidence_items.source_quote: Leptospira microscopic agglutination test (MAT) became positive with a high titer.

rationale: A 55-year-old male paddy field worker developed severe pulmonary hemorrhage, AKI, and ischemic bowel necrosis. Leptospira MAT was confirmed positive with a high titer (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old male presenting with fever, severe pulmonary hemorrhage, and bowel necrosis after working in paddy fields

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by microscopic agglutination test (MAT) at 1:640 titer

evidence_items.source_quote: Leptospira MAT was positive at a titer of 1 : 640.

rationale: A 52-year-old male paddy field worker developed severe pulmonary hemorrhage, oliguric AKI, and ischemic bowel necrosis. Microscopic agglutination test (MAT) was positive at a high titer of 1:640 (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 14-year-old male presenting with fever, oliguria, and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES)

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by microscopic agglutination test (MAT) at 1:160 titer

evidence_items.source_quote: Leptospirosis was confirmed with a microscopic agglutination test (MAT) titre of 1:160.

rationale: A 14-year-old male with stagnant water exposure in a paddy field presented with fever, AKI, and PRES. Leptospirosis was confirmed by MAT with a titer of 1:160 in an endemic clinical context, with complete recovery after IV ceftriaxone (E2). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 49-year-old male construction worker presenting with acute abdominal pain, jaundice, and alveolar hemorrhage after flood exposure

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by ELISA-IgM and MAT for serovar Cynopteri at 1/800 titer

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory investigation confirmed leptospirosis by two consecutive serological tests: ELISA-IgM and a microscopic agglutination test for the serovar Cynopteri, with a titer of 1/800. He was treated with ceftriaxone for 14 days, leading to clinical and laboratory improvement.

rationale: A 49-year-old male presented with fever, acute abdomen, AKI, and alveolar hemorrhage following floodwater ingestion. Acute leptospirosis was confirmed by positive ELISA-IgM and MAT (1/800 for serovar Cynopteri) (E1). Subsequent secondary gastrointestinal mucormycosis developed as a complication. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 60-year-old male farmer presenting with fever, convulsions, and multifocal CNS lesions

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by CSF metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS)

evidence_items.source_quote: Cerebrospinal fluid Metagenomic Next-generation Sequencing (mNGS) confirmed leptospiral infection. Empirical antibiotics were adjusted from intravenous vancomycin (1000 mg q12h) and intravenous meropenem (1000 mg q8h) to definitive penicillin sodium (40 WU q8h). The patient achieved marked clinical improvement within two weeks, with follow-up MRI showing a significant reduction of the CNS lesions and chest CT revealing marked resolution of pulmonary infiltrates (Fig. 3, Fig. 4).

rationale: A 60-year-old male farmer presented with fever, recurrent generalized seizures, and multifocal inflammatory CNS lesions. Metagenomic NGS of cerebrospinal fluid confirmed Leptospira infection, with rapid clinical improvement on penicillin (E1). VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 69-year-old male farmer presenting with severe pneumonia, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and ARDS requiring VV-ECMO

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospira interrogans confirmed by mNGS of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and blood

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 3, mNGS confirmed Leptospira interrogans infection, with a coverage rate of 1% and a relative abundance of 16.45% (Figure 1D).

rationale: A 69-year-old farmer presented with dyspnea, severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, and refractory hypoxemia requiring VV-ECMO. Metagenomic NGS confirmed Leptospira interrogans infection with 16.45% relative abundance (E1), and the patient recovered successfully. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 72-year-old male farmer presenting with calf pain, hemoptysis, and severe diffuse alveolar hemorrhage requiring VV-ECMO

step5_concept_grounding: Leptospirosis confirmed by mNGS testing of blood and lavage fluid

evidence_items.source_quote: Both blood and lavage fluid were sent for mNGS testing. On day 3, mNGS confirmed leptospirosis, and platelet transfusion (10 U) was administered on day 4, but a follow-up chest CT showed worsening pulmonary hemorrhage (Figure 2B).

rationale: A 72-year-old farmer presented with fever, bilateral calf pain, hemoptysis, and life-threatening ARDS with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage requiring VV-ECMO. Metagenomic NGS of blood and lavage fluid confirmed Leptospira infection on day 3 (E1), and the patient achieved full recovery. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.
